      How this works

      Claude reads each document on its own and returns only what is printed, with the exact text it copied. The page checks the 15 required elements, data conventions, whether each quote is really on the page, and whether the documents name the same patient.

      When every check passes, the case moves to coverage review on its own. Coverage uses the card from the order or the plan on file. With neither, the agent texts a mobile number a secure link; a landline gets a call from the voice assistant instead.

      A covered drug that needs prior authorization moves to the PA step. The agent pulls the plan's criteria, answers each ePA question only from the documents with a link to the source, and leaves anything it can't support blank. A clearance rep reviews the sourced answers and submits with one click. The agent reads the payer's decision, reruns the claim and hands the case to the RPh.

      Anything missing, unclear or conflicting on the prescription goes to the pharmacist (RPh) for a clarification check. Coverage and PA exceptions go to a clearance rep. The agent never invents data, never submits a PA, and never clears a prescription to ship.

      Sample result. The document readings in this case are pre-written examples, not AI. The checks, coverage, PA preparation and your decisions all run for real on this page. Connect your key to have Claude read the documents.

            Evals: five test cases, one framework

            Run each case, read what the agent actually did, and choose the verdict yourself. The page never grades itself. For case 1, finish the human steps in the workspace (review, submit, bring in the payer's decision) and the actual result updates. Results are kept for this visit only, so copy them before you leave.

            Evaluation framework

            Five criteria, measured by the page from the evidence of each run: what the agent read before any human edit, whether each quote is really on the cited page, where the case stopped, and who submitted. The metrics describe the run. The verdict for each case is still yours.
